title: Yonger Bastida Rejects AJ Ferrari Apology and Demands RAF Rematch - NewsBreak
text:
By Adityan Pillai ,
1 hours ago
Mar 20, 2026; Cleveland, OH, USA; Iowa State Cyclones Yonger Bastida reacts after competing against Nebraska Cornhuskers AJ Ferrari during the NCAA DI Wrestling Championship at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images
Yonger Bastida responded to AJ Ferrari’s recent apology, and honestly, he wasn’t buying it. He kept his cool, but made it pretty clear that just saying sorry doesn’t really cut it. Instead of getting caught up in the back-and-forth, he brought the attention right back to what actually matters, the wrestling.
Yonger Bastida Challenges AJ Ferrari to a Rematch After NCAA Controversy It all started after their match at the 2026 NCAA Wrestling Championships. Bastida won 15-7 in the heavyweight semifinal, and Ferrari did not take it well. In his post-match press conference, he started raising eyebrows about how much Bastida’s body had changed, even bringing up his size and acne as reasons to question what was behind it.
Ferrari later addressed the backlash with a public statement, saying he “was not at all saying that he is on HGH” and clarified that his comments were general and meant jokingly. He added that all his opponents, including Bastida, deserved respect, while expressing regret if his words were misunderstood.
READ MORE: AJ Ferrari Clarifies ‘Facetious’ HGH Remarks Toward Iowa State’s Yonger Bastida
Days after the NCAA Championships kept stirring up noise, Ferrari decided to step up and address it head-on. Addressing the situation publicly, he shared a more positive update after speaking directly with Bastida, saying :
“I just got off the phone with Yonger, and we’re both excited to embrace the future and the opportunities ahead of us. Respect, integrity, and faith are important to both of us. We remain great friends and have deep respect for each other, both on and off the wrestling mat.”
Despite acknowledging Ferrari’s apology, Bastida made it clear that he isn’t interested in settling things through statements alone. He called for a rematch, straight up, sending the message that respect isn’t handed out in statements; it’s earned through competition.
He made his point one more time and put it out there plain and simple :
“Respect for the apology! But let’s be real, words don’t fix what happened. If you really want to clear the air, step on the mat one more time with me at a RAF event. No noise, no talking, “NO EXCUSES,” just WRESTLING. That’s where respect is earned for real. I’m not here for drama.”
The hype is building, and RAF 07 is locked in for March 28, 2026, in Tampa, Florida, but a Bastida vs. Ferrari rematch hasn’t been confirmed just yet. On top of all this, after defeating Ferrari, Bastida reached the NCAA Championships final but came up short, losing to Isaac Trumble for the title.
